slots.hypothesis: Unchanged and passed at audit 1 (novelty 4, soundness 4). Hypothesis: overnight vs intraday return attribution. ON = log(open/prev close), ID = log(close/open). The slot uses: the ON-ID difference, single legs, a dimensionless version, cs_regres(ON, ID), and cross_corr / cross_regbeta of ON vs ID, over 60-241 days. Kept byte-for-byte; the auditor struck seed 1 (rev 0.53), so 13 of 14 seeds remain.

Rewritten after audit 1 (soundness 2, all 10 seeds failed the gate). Same idea: net tradable share supply over the past year, i.e. composite issuance (Daniel-Titman 2006) / net payout yield (Boudoukh et al. 2007). It rests on the exact identity sub(LogFloatCap|LogTotalCap, log(day_last(Close))) = log shares - log back-adjustment factor + const. New implementation, per the auditor: NaN-safe accumulation ts_sum(ts_delta(x, 1), 241) instead of ts_delta(x, d>=60), so coverage matches the leaf. The 60/120-day versions are dropped and every window is 241 days. Seeds without events sit on a float32 grid of a few ulps (at most ~a dozen distinct values per day), so distinct >= 0.5 needs real events. The |value|<1e-4 share is given only as a prior: 0.2-0.3 in steady state, 0.4-0.6 in Jun-Jul and early train. The long-only leg (direction -1) is stated outright: it is the highest trailing net-payout-yield stocks, mostly dividend yield, with issuance and unlocks counted negative. The lock-ratio level term is kept in one seed only. 8 seeds: float/total 241-day accumulations, their 20- and 60-day means, cs_regres(float, total) as the unlock component, and lock ratio + total issuance.

result.summary:
The plan is rewritten and the check passes: `c06_check.py 807 2` prints ADMISSIBLE, exit 0. Only the parts that failed audit 1 changed; slot a and R groups 1, 2 and 4 are byte-identical (checked by comparing the parsed YAML against the old plan).

Slot b (still N, same idea: net share supply / composite issuance) has 8 new seeds, none reused from the struck ones. They follow the auditor's fix:
- The accumulation is ts_sum(ts_delta(sub(LogFloatCap|LogTotalCap, log(day_last(Close))), 1), 241). It returns NaN only when all 241 days are missing, so coverage should match the leaf. The old 60/120/241-day ts_delta needed a value exactly d rows back, which is why coverage failed.
- The 60/120-day versions are gone; every window is 241 days.
- distinct: a stock with no corporate action in the year only takes values within a few float32 ulps of zero (at most about a dozen distinct values per day). So distinct >= 0.5 can only come from real events, not rounding noise.
- The auditor asked for the share of values with |value| < 1e-4. I could not compute it: there is no local data and the PI does not run the server. The plan gives a prior instead: 0.2-0.3 in steady state, 0.4-0.6 in June-July and in the first months of train. The new table's gate column will be the actual check.
- The hypothesis now says plainly that the direction -1 long decile is the highest trailing net-payout-yield stocks, which for most names is just dividend yield. It differs only in counting issuance and unlocks as negative and pricing dividends at the ex-date. I added Boudoukh et al. 2007 (JF 62(2), April 2007; repec URL checked) as the source.
- The lock-ratio level term (0.42 with head 8) appears in one seed only.

R3 is deleted rather than rewritten. Its variant 1 was only diagnostic, and the table's residual |rho| of 0.85 already answers that question. Its issuance variants duplicate slot b, and if one were added to the library it could block slot b's own seeds. That leaves 3 R groups and 6 variants.

The auditor suggested dropping R1 variant 2 and R2 variant 3 (explicit volatility null controls). I left them in because those groups passed and the instructions say to keep passed parts unchanged. The notebook records this.

The notebook's round-2 section has a new subsection explaining what changed and why. It also adds one prediction: at least 6 of the 8 slot-b seeds pass the gate (0.75); if the 241-day accumulation still fails distinct, the third draft switches to a different idea.
